brief:
Today, 3 November, is Legs A at the New York gym, your first Legs A there, and the last of the six nights to run on these machines. Tomorrow, 4 November, the rotation goes to Push B (not Push A; Push A ran on 28 October, and the order after Legs A is Push B). The 2 November Pull A is in and read: 21 of 21 sets in 56 minutes, the first Pull A you have ever finished in full, and every slot held its rep range; three were under the card’s number (the seated row at 10 where the card asked 12, the first two deadlift sets ramping up from 205 where it asked 235 on all four, the first face-pull set at 27 where it asked 32.5) and the hammer curl went past it. Deadlift 205, 225, 235, 240 for 5, four sets, logged as you went; wide pulldown 105 for 10 then 120 for 8, 8; seated row 105 for 10 on all four; dumbbell curl 30 for 9, 9, 9; cable hammer curl 39 for 13 then 42.5 for 11, 10 (the card asked 35 and you went past it); face pulls 27 for 12 then 32.5 for 12; cable lateral raise 10 for 12, 12. One program change today, version 7: the calf press on Legs A moves up to fifth, before the hip machines, because it has been skipped on the last two leg nights and the hip machines are the lowest-value sets on a night that has to end on time. Nothing else moves: the Pull A night argues for nothing structural, and the one question you wrote on it is answered below, not acted on.

You asked on the seated row, “Why four sets?” Here is the honest answer. The row went from three sets to four on 1 August because Pull A gives your biceps six direct sets (dumbbell curl 3, hammer curl 3) and your back two pulls plus the deadlift, and the back day should row at least as much as it curls. Whether the upper back is at its floor or over its ceiling depends on how sets are counted, and that is the open question dated 9 November: counting only the lifts that work it directly, this row and the Pull B chest-supported row are eight sets, exactly the floor of eight; counting half a set from every pulldown, deadlift, face pull and pec deck as the targets were written, it is 19.5 against a ceiling of 16. The fourth set of this row is decided with that rule on 9 November, from the New York log. Until then it stays at four: on 2 November you did all four at 105 for 10, each set exactly 10, about two and a half minutes apart, and nothing fell off, so it is work you can do, and the reason it was added still holds. If you would rather carry three now, write it in the note and the next morning’s review answers it.

Tonight, Legs A, 20 sets, every number in pounds, and these are the numbers written for you yesterday, unchanged, because nothing new has been logged on a leg machine since 30 October. Leg press, feet low: 180 for 10, 190 for 10, then 200 for 8, logged as you go (160, 180, 200 for 10, 10, 8 on this press on 30 October, typed in afterwards); 200 is the one set to test, not a weight to hold for three, and when all three sets reach 10 the plate moves. Split squat: 20 lb dumbbells for 10 each leg, two sets. Leg curl: 135 for 10, then 150 for 10, 10 (120, 135, 150 for 10 on this machine on 30 October). Leg extension: 150 for 12, two sets (150 then 157.5 for 10 on this machine on 30 October in the squat slot). Adductor 80 for 12 and abductor 60 for 12, two sets each, as starting points on stacks you have not logged (your August home-gym machines took 105 and 135; if these read like that, go there on the first set and log it); they come after the calf press tonight. Calf press on the leg press, now fifth on the card, before the hip machines: 250 for 12, three sets, a starting point read off the leg-press numbers, not a measured one; if 250 for 12 is easy, go to 280 on the second set and log it. Adductor and abductor after it. Cable crunch: 52.5 for 12, three sets (52.5 for 12, 10, 10 on this stack on 30 October). If time runs short, the order is: the leg press, split squat and leg curl are not cut; drop the abductor first, then the adductor.

The calf press has been skipped on the last two leg nights (Chennai on 14 October, New York on 30 October) so today it moves earlier on Legs A (program version 7), and its decision is dated tomorrow morning, 4 November: logged tonight and the slot stays on both leg nights as it is; skipped again, from fifth on the card, and it becomes the standing or seated calf machine this gym has, with your note on which exists. It does not go without a replacement.

Tomorrow, Push B, 20 sets: shoulder press 50 lb dumbbells for 10 on all four sets, up from the 45 you pressed for 8, 10, 10, 10 on 31 October (Chennai was 25 kg, about 55 lb, for 8 and 9 on 15 October, so 50 is the step back toward that); machine chest press 135 for 10 on all three sets, logged as you go (135 for 12 on Push A on 28 October was typed in from memory, and a new plate is not written off a remembered set; 150 is next once 135 for 10 is logged live); dumbbell lateral raise 15 for 15, three sets; high-to-low crossover 29 for 15, two sets; reverse pec deck 90 for 13, three sets (90 for 13, 12, 12 on the Push A machine on 28 October; skipped on the last two Push B nights, and skipped again it comes off Push B); rope pushdown 47.5 for 12, three sets; and the last slot at 50 for 12, two sets, which is where you wrote “Overhead db press” on 31 October. On that last one, write a single word in the note tomorrow, “triceps” if it was one dumbbell held overhead in both hands, “press” if it was two dumbbells pressed, and the slot becomes the lift you name. The second coach’s audit this morning read the log as one dumbbell held overhead (two 50s pressed for 12, 12 after four sets of 45s is not likely) and asked the trainer to write the extension outright; that stays open, because yesterday’s audit found the opposite fault and the slot is not flipped twice on reasoning alone, so until you write the word the card shows 50 for 12 under the name you typed and the program still lists the reverse-grip pushdown beneath it. Tomorrow’s numbers are written into the card now so they are there even if tomorrow morning’s review fails to reach the app; tomorrow’s review re-reads them against tonight.

Two things still stand from the 31 October card. The names you type on a card stick to that slot at this gym: the Legs B squat card reads Leg Extension, the Push B last card reads Overhead db press and the Push A lateral-raise card reads Db lateral raise until you blank the name field. And no bodyweight has been logged since 23 August (207 lb); a morning weigh-in this week would anchor the block.

One open item read against the new night: whether this New York gym is the one you trained at in August. The 29 October Pull B matched 25 August to the pound; the 2 November Pull A is mixed, with the wide pulldown at 120 for 8 against 150 for 10 on 28 August, the seated row at 105 for 10s against 105 for 12s, the hammer curl at 42.5 against 35, and the face pulls at 32.5 against 27.5. It stays open, and August numbers stay quoted, not prescribed.

Where this leaves the week: 118 days to the show, day seven of the first week of this block (build to 24 November, deload 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December). Five of the six New York nights are in; tonight makes it one full pass on one set of machines, which is the whole reason the block was restarted here. The counting question behind the muscles that read over their ceilings on paper is still dated 9 November, after the second Pull B and Push B have shown whether the fourth shrug set and the Push B pec deck run.

block.why: One new night since the last review: Pull A on 2 November at New York, 21 of 21 sets in 56 minutes, the first Pull A in the log finished in full (the best before was 19 sets, on 18 and 28 August, when Pull A asked 20), with every slot inside its rep range, three of them under the card’s number (row 10 not 12, the first two deadlift sets ramped from 205, the first face-pull set 27) and one above it (hammer curl 42.5 against 35): deadlift 205, 225, 235, 240 for 5 on four sets, logged live three to four minutes apart; wide pulldown 105 for 10 then 120 for 8, 8; seated row 105 for 10 on all four; dumbbell curl 30 for 9, 9, 9; hammer curl 39 for 13 then 42.5 for 11, 10 against a card that asked 35; face pulls 27 for 12 then 32.5 for 12; cable lateral raise 10 for 12, 12. Meso 3 restarted on 28 October at this gym; today is the seventh day of its first week (build to 24 November, deload 25 November to 1 December, assessment 2 to 8 December, prep from 9 December; the show is 118 days away). Five of the six nights have now run here (Push A 28 October, Pull B 29 October, Legs B 30 October, Push B 31 October, Pull A 2 November); Legs A tonight completes the first pass on one set of machines, and tomorrow is Push B by the rotation. One program change today, version 7: the Legs A calf press moves from seventh to fifth, ahead of the hip machines, because it was skipped on the last two leg nights (Chennai 14 October, New York 30 October, where the crunch ran and the calf press did not) and the hip machines are the lowest-value four sets on a night that has to end on time; Legs A stays at 20 sets and no weekly count moves. The rest stays as version 6 wrote it on 1 November (one dips slot, on Push A; Push B without its dips slot and with the rope pushdown in the overhead slot; the assisted-dips and overhead-cable-extension slots left the program that day and are not reviewed below). Nothing else changes, and this is the reason: the one night in argues for no structural change, every Pull A slot held its rep range or beat it, and the one question on it (“Why four sets?” on the seated row) is answered rather than acted on, because the row went to four on 1 August so the back day rows at least as much as it curls, the night shows four at 105 for 10 is work he can do, and whether the upper back is at its floor (direct count) or over its ceiling (weighted count) is the counting rule dated 9 November, which decides the fourth set with it. A note from him asking for three now would be the new fact that changes it sooner. Tonight’s Legs A numbers are the ones written yesterday, unchanged, because no leg machine has been logged since 30 October; tomorrow’s Push B numbers are written into the card now. The 4-week averages in this review count the current week, which has one night in it, so fourteen of the eighteen read lower than yesterday’s (the window moving, not the training); the four the 2 November Pull A fed rose or held (side delts 5.1 to 5.3, lats 8.5 to 8.8, biceps 8.9 to 9, traps 3.5). Dated items: the calves decision is tomorrow morning, 4 November, after tonight’s Legs A; the counting-rule question behind nine muscles that read over their ceilings on paper stays dated 9 November, after the second Pull B and Push B show whether the fourth shrug set and the Push B pec deck run. Watched without a date: the Push B reverse pec deck (skipped two of the last three Push B nights), the fourth shrug set, the Push A lateral-raise slot (dumbbells on 28 October), the reverse-grip slot (two sets logged as an overhead dumbbell press). The next boundary is the deload on 25 November: sets drop to about 60% and each load drops about a fifth, rounded down to the lift’s step, and the prep block is written at the assessment from what these four weeks log.

chest.why: Eighteen direct sets a rotation (Push A: incline 4, chest press 3, crossover 3, dips 3; Push B: chest press 3, crossover 2), exactly the ceiling of 18, unchanged since the 1 November push-day change. Push A is the chest-led night with 13 and Push B the shoulder-led night with 5, on purpose. 7.5 a week done over four weeks (that window now counts this week, which has only the 2 November Pull A in it). New York chest nights so far: 28 October (incline 175 for 6, chest press 135 for 12, crossover 12.5 for 12s, typed in from memory) and 31 October (a smith bench 185 for 8, 8, 8 in the old dips slot and the high-to-low crossover 29 for 15, 13, logged live; the machine chest press skipped). Tomorrow’s Push B is the chest press’s heavy day: 135 for 10 on all three, logged live, and 150 once that is on the log.

front-delts.why: Eight direct sets (incline press 4, Push B shoulder press 4), inside the direct range of 4 to 10; the 15 on paper is those 8 plus half a set from every chest press, both crossovers and the dips, which is the counting question dated 9 November. 7.1 a week done over four weeks. The shoulder press ran at New York on 31 October: 45 lb dumbbells for 8, 10, 10, 10, four sets in range, logged live, 10 lb under the 25 kg (55 lb) you pressed for 8 and 9 at Chennai on 15 October. Tomorrow it goes to 50 for 10 on all four, the step back toward 55.

side-delts.why: Eight direct sets a rotation (Push A raise 3, Push B dumbbell raise 3, the Pull A cable raise 2 added on 26 October) plus half credit from the Push B press, 10 on paper, against a floor of 8 direct. 5.3 a week done over four weeks. All three slots now have a New York night: the Push A slot ran as dumbbell lateral raises on 28 October (12.5 for 12s, typed in), the Push B dumbbell raise on 31 October (15 for 15, 13, 13, logged live), and the Pull A cable raise on 2 November, 10 for 12, 12, its first night there, done between the curls rather than after the face pulls where the card puts it. Still watching rather than changing: the Push A slot has not yet been done on the machine it names, and until it is, which lift that slot is stays open (see that lift).

rear-delts.why: Ten direct sets (reverse pec deck 3 and 3, face pulls 2 and 2), inside the direct range of 6 to 12; the 15.5 on paper is half credit from the wide pulldown and both rows (the close pulldown and the straight-arm carry none) (dated 9 November). 5.8 a week done over four weeks. The Push A pec deck ran on 28 October, 90 for 13, 12, 12. Face pulls have now run on both pull nights at New York: 27.5 for 15, 15 on 29 October, then 27 for 12 and 32.5 for 12 on 2 November, so the step to 32.5 is on the stack. The Push B pec deck was skipped on 31 October and on 15 October at Chennai, two of the last three Push B nights; tomorrow it sits fifth of seven on a 20-set night and gets its one more chance: skipped again and it comes off Push B, with its three sets going to a rear-delt lift chosen that morning from the catalogue, not to a third face-pull set (you wrote on 28 August, “Why three? I think two”, and the program cut them to two on 3 September, so that stays).

lats.why: Seventeen direct sets on paper (wide pulldown 3, seated row 4, chest-supported row 4, close pulldown 3, straight-arm 3), 18 with the rollout’s half credit, at the ceiling of 18. 8.8 a week done over four weeks. Both pull nights have now run at New York: Pull B on 29 October (close pulldown 112.5 for 10 then 127.5 for 9, 9; straight-arm 45 for 9 then 37.5 for 10, 10; chest-supported row 50 for 8s) and Pull A on 2 November (wide pulldown 105 for 10 then 120 for 8, 8; seated row 105 for 10 on all four), every set inside its range except the straight-arm’s opener at 45 for 9, which was dropped to 37.5 on the spot. Held: the lats are at the ceiling on paper and every lift is still finding its New York number.

upper-back.why: Eight direct sets (seated row 4, chest-supported dumbbell row 4), the floor of the direct range 8 to 16; the 19.5 on paper is half credit from both pulldowns, the deadlift, the RDL, both face-pull slots and both reverse pec decks (dated 9 November). 7.9 a week done over four weeks. Both rows have run at New York: the chest-supported row 50 lb a hand for 8, 8, 8, 8 on 29 October, and the seated row 105 for 10 on all four sets on 2 November, where you asked “Why four sets?”. The answer: the row went to four on 1 August so the back day rows at least as much as it curls (six biceps sets on Pull A); by the direct count these two rows are the floor of eight, by the weighted count the targets were written for the upper back is 19.5 against a ceiling of 16, and that rule, dated 9 November, decides the fourth set. Held at four until then; a note asking for three is answered the next morning.

traps.why: Four direct shrug sets planned since 26 October, the direct floor of 4; the rest of the 9.5 on paper is half credit from the deadlift, both face-pull slots and the Push A machine lateral raise (the dumbbell and cable raises carry none). The first night of four sets, 29 October, ran three: 80 lb dumbbells for 15, 15, 15. 3.5 a week done over four weeks. The 2 November deadlift (240 for 5) and face pulls added half credit, nothing direct. No Pull B since 29 October, so the shrug question is unchanged: if the next Pull B also stops at three, the fourth set comes off rather than staying on paper.

lower-back.why: No direct slot: the 3.5 on paper is half credit from the deadlift (4) and the barbell RDL (3). Held without a direct lift on purpose; a heavy deadlift and a barbell RDL in the same week are the lower-back work. The deadlift ran on 2 November, 205, 225, 235, 240 for 5 on four sets, the first New York hinge; the RDL has still not run here (skipped on 30 October), so the next Legs B is the first.

biceps.why: Eleven direct sets (dumbbell curl 3, hammer 3, incline curl 2, reverse curl 3), inside the direct range of 8 to 14; the 18 on paper adds half a set from each pull (dated 9 November). 9 a week done over four weeks. Both pull nights have run at New York: incline curl 25 for 10 then 30 for 9 and reverse curl 27.5 then 32.5 for 10, 10, 10 on 29 October; dumbbell curl 30 for 9, 9, 9 and hammer curl 39 for 13 then 42.5 for 11, 10 on 2 November, where the card asked 35 and you went past it. The curls are moving; held.

triceps.why: Eight direct sets after the 1 November change (dips 3 on Push A, rope pushdown 3 and reverse-grip pushdown 2 on Push B), the floor of the direct range 8 to 14; the 16.5 on paper adds half a set from the incline, two chest presses, the shoulder press and the straight-arm pulldown, which is why it still reads over the ceiling (dated 9 November). 9.8 a week done over four weeks, the best-served muscle in the log by that count, so eight direct sets plus four pressing lifts is enough for now. What you did at New York: dips 8, 10, 12 on 28 October; rope pushdown 42.5 for 12 then 47.5 for 12, 10 on 31 October; and two sets logged as “Overhead db press”, 50 for 12, 12, in the reverse-grip slot, under a name the trainer cannot place on its own (one dumbbell overhead is a triceps extension that fits the slot; two pressed is a second shoulder press), so tomorrow’s Push B asks you which it was (see that lift).

forearms.why: Six direct sets (hammer and reverse curls), inside the direct range of 2 to 8; the 12 on paper adds half a set from the dumbbell curl, the shrugs, the reverse-grip pushdown and the RDL (dated 9 November). 5.3 a week done over four weeks. Reverse curl 32.5 for 10s on 29 October; hammer curl 39 for 13 then 42.5 for 11, 10 on 2 November, above the 35 the card asked. Held.

quads.why: Thirteen direct sets a rotation (Legs A press 3, split squat 2, leg extension 2; Legs B smith squat 3, feet-low press 3), inside 10 to 18, unchanged. 2.8 a week done over four weeks, the largest shortfall against a floor of any muscle (7.2 under 10), and 30 October was the only quad night since 14 October: leg press 160, 180, 200 for 10, 10, 8 (all three typed in within 12 seconds, so recalled) and leg extension 150, 157.5, 157.5 for 10 in the squat slot because the smith was taken (the first two typed 7 seconds apart). Tonight is Legs A, four days after that night, with the press, split squat and extension; the two leg nights then run three days apart from here (Legs A, then Push B, Pull B, Legs B).

hamstrings.why: Thirteen direct sets (deadlift 4, barbell RDL 3, two leg curls 6), inside 8 to 14; the 15.5 on paper adds half credit from the split squat and smith squat (dated 9 November). 3.9 a week done over four weeks. Leg curl at New York on 30 October: 120, 135, 150 for 10, 10, 10, logged live; the deadlift on 2 November: 205, 225, 235, 240 for 5, four sets, logged live, the first New York hinge. The RDL has not run here yet (skipped on 30 October). Tonight’s leg curl: 135 for 10, then 150 for 10, 10.

glutes.why: Twelve direct sets (deadlift 4, split squat 2, RDL 3, smith squat 3), inside 6 to 14; the 16 on paper adds half credit from two leg presses and the abductor (dated 9 November). 3.8 a week done over four weeks. The 2 November deadlift (240 for 5 on the top set, four sets) is the first direct glute night at New York; neither the RDL nor the smith squat ran on 30 October (skipped; smith taken). Tonight’s split squat, 20 lb for 10 each leg, is the second.

adductors.why: Two direct sets on Legs A, the floor of 2 to 6; the 7.5 on paper adds half credit from the leg presses, smith squat and split squat, which is why it reads over the ceiling (dated 9 November). 1.4 a week done over four weeks. Tonight is the first New York night for the adductor machine: 80 for 12 is the starting point from Singapore’s 80 for 15 on 5 October; the August home-gym machine took 105 for 12s on 20 August, and if this stack reads like that, go there on the first set and log it.

abductors.why: Two planned, exactly the floor, all on Legs A. 0 a week done over four weeks: last 60 for 15, 15 at Singapore on 5 October, skipped at Chennai on 14 October, and no Legs A since. Tonight is the first New York night: 60 for 12 is the starting point, the same rule as the adductor (the last machine logged); the August home-gym machine took 135 for 13s on 20 August, so if this stack reads like that, go there on the first set. If tonight runs short it is the first slot to drop, because the adductor and the leg press carry the hips.

calves.why: Six direct sets a rotation (calf press on the leg press, 3 on Legs A and 3 on Legs B), exactly the floor of 6. 0.8 a week done over four weeks, and still no calf work since Singapore on 5 October (290 for 15, 12 then 270 for 14): the Legs B calf press was skipped on 30 October, in a 29-minute night that also skipped the RDL at the start, so this reads as a short night rather than a missing machine. Today it moves from seventh to fifth on Legs A, before the hip machines, so it is not the slot that runs out of time (program version 7; on Legs B it already sits last behind the abs by the 13 October order, on purpose, because calves are also trained here). The decision is dated tomorrow morning, 4 November, after tonight’s Legs A: logged tonight and the slot stays on both leg nights; skipped again from fifth and it becomes the standing or seated calf machine this gym has, with your note on which exists. It does not go without a replacement.

abs.why: Eight planned (cable crunch 3 and 3, ab wheel rollout 2). 2 a week done over four weeks. Both ran on 30 October at New York, logged live: ab wheel 8, 8 from the knees on its first night, cable crunch 52.5 for 12, 10, 10 on this stack. Tonight’s Legs A crunch holds 52.5 and chases 12 on all three.

smith-incline-press.why: On 28 October at New York: 155, 175, 175 for 6 each, typed in within 11 seconds at the start of a 10-minute logging window, so remembered, not logged set by set; three sets, not the four asked. Singapore on 6 October was 75 kg (165 lb) for 6s on a different smith bar; the home gym ran 180 for 8 on 27 August. No Push A since. Next Push A: 175 for 6 on all four sets, logged as you go; four logged sets at 8 earn 180.

machine-chest-press.why: First New York night 28 October on Push A: 105, 120, 135 for 12 each, typed in within 11 seconds, so remembered. On 31 October the Push B slot was skipped and a smith bench done in the old dips slot instead (185 for 8s), so this press has one New York night on one of its two days. It stays on both: Push A 10 to 12 (hold 135 for 12, three sets, logged live), Push B 8 to 10, its heavy day, tomorrow: 135 for 10 on all three, logged live, because the 28 October sets were remembered and a new plate is not earned off a remembered set; three live sets of 10 at 135 earn 150, the next plate this machine showed (105, 120, 135 are 15 apart).

cable-crossover-low-high.why: First New York night: 12.5 for 12, 12, 12 on 28 October, all three typed in within 1.3 seconds, so remembered. Singapore was 10 for 15s on a different stack. Hold 12.5 next Push A and log each set as it is done; 15s on all three earns the next plate on that stack.

machine-lateral-raise.why: In the program since 13 October and never once done as itself: on 28 October the slot ran as dumbbell lateral raises, 12.5 lb for 12, 12, 12 (typed in within 1.3 seconds), and that name now sits on this card at New York until you blank it. Whether the gym has a lateral raise machine is not in the log. If the next Push A is dumbbells again, the slot becomes what you actually do; since Push B already has the dumbbell raise (15 for 15, 13, 13 on 31 October), it would become a cable raise or a different angle, not a duplicate. Next Push A: 12.5 for 12, three sets, on the machine if there is one, dumbbells if not, and say which in the note.

reverse-pec-deck.why: Push A on 28 October at New York: 90 for 13, 12, 12, logged live. Push B on 31 October: skipped, as it was at Chennai on 15 October, two of the last three Push B nights (12 October it was 50 kg for 11s). The dossier calls it stalled; that is arithmetic across four gyms’ machines. Hold 90 on Push A and chase 15s. Tomorrow’s Push B, 20 sets with this fifth of seven, is its one more chance: 90 for 13, three sets; skipped again and it comes off Push B.

chest-dip.why: In the program since 1 November as the one dips slot, on Push A where you did bar dips on 28 October (8, 10, 12 at bodyweight, in the overhead-extension slot, no note). Earlier bar dips: 10, 10, 10 at Warsaw on 30 September, 8, 8 on 22 September; bench dips ran 17 to 19 at the home gym and Chennai. Three sets of 8 to 12 bar dips, chest lean; next Push A 10, 10, 10, and 12 on all three earns a slower tempo or added weight. This is the catalogue’s bar-dip id, chosen because the old dips id carries the name you typed on it at New York on 31 October (“Smith bench”) and would have shown that name on the Push A card.

deadlift.why: A barbell weighs the same at every gym, so this is the one lift whose numbers compare across the whole log. On 2 November at New York: 205, 225, 235, 240 for 5, four sets, logged live three to four minutes apart, against a card that asked 235 on all four. That is the third visit up in a row since the sick Singapore night: 225 for 6 on 8 October, 235 for 5, 5, 5 at Vancouver on 23 October (three sets), 240 for 5 now, and the first four-set deadlift since 8 October. August was heavier (255 for 6, 6 on 18 August, 265 for 5, 5 on 28 August), and the gap is the road back. The dossier says regressing against the trailing median; that median is the August nights, and the direction since October is up. Next Pull A: 225 for 5, then 240 for 5, 5, 5; the last three sets at 6, the top of the range, earn 250.

lat-pulldown-wide.why: First New York number, 2 November, logged live about two minutes apart: 105 for 10, then 120 for 8, 8, exactly the card, and 120 for 8 is the bottom of the 8 to 10 range. The card said to go to 135 if 105 was clearly easy; you did not, so 120 is the working weight on this stack. Vancouver on 23 October was 105, 110, 120 for 9, 9, 8 on a different stack. Next Pull A: 120 for 9 on all three; three sets at 10 earn 127.5.

seated-cable-row-wide.why: First New York number, 2 November, logged live about two and a half minutes apart: 105 for 10, 10, 10, 10, every set exactly the bottom of the 10 to 12 range, with the note “Why four sets?”. The card asked 12 and you got 10 on every set, the bottom of the range, with nothing falling off, so 105 is the right weight and not yet an easy one. The four sets stay for now: the row went to four on 1 August so the back day rows at least as much as it curls (six biceps sets on Pull A, against this row, the wide pulldown and the deadlift’s half credit), and whether that leaves the upper back at its floor (direct count, eight of eight) or over its ceiling (weighted count, 19.5 against 16) is the counting rule dated 9 November, which decides the fourth set with it. If you would rather carry three now, write it in the note. Next Pull A: 105 for 11 on all four; four sets at 12 earn 112.5.
